explanation: This page lists the takeaways and assignments for the lesson. Students are instructed to examine historical papers from the studied experiments (such as Griffith, Avery, Hershey-Chase, and Watson-Crick) and write observations in their lab notebooks comparing the structure, look, and tone of these older scientific publications to the modern papers they read in Journal Club and ITR. Specifically, students are told to read the Watson and Crick paper, paying attention to its simple tone and concise presentation of information. Finally, students must complete a sticky note on the class Jamboard.

questions.q: What notebook assignment is given to students regarding historical scientific papers?
opts: Compare the structure, look, and tone of historical papers to modern journal club papers.
Translate the papers into another language.
Write a 5-page summary of each paper.
questions.exp: Option B is correct because the slide directs students to 'Write in your lab notebook a few observations between these historical papers compared to papers you have read for Journal Club & ITR' focusing on 'Structure, look, tone, etc.' The other options are incorrect.
